text: What happened next is one small verse, and it holds the whole man.
He threw off his cloak, jumped up, and came.
That cloak was a beggar's entire world — his coat, his bed at night, the very thing he spread out to catch the coins he lived on.
A blind man who throws his cloak behind him may never find it again.
He threw it anyway, coins and all.
He spent everything he owned on the chance that the shout had been heard.
